analysis:
Examined the changed files in this batch. JinjaSanitizationTests.swift adds a single unit test (head lines 77-91, testLeafFastPathKeepsDynamicTypesAndUnwrapsBoxedOptionals) covering the sanitizeForJinja leaf fast path. It checks that dynamic leaf types are preserved and that boxed Optionals are unwrapped or dropped. It is test-only, with no runtime or security-boundary change. The base and head units otherwise match apart from line renumbering.

PromptTokenCacheTests.swift is a new test file (455 lines). Only the patch excerpt was supplied and it is truncated, so unit b1b4dab7a21c3b0d:0 has no visible body and I could not read it. The visible portion contains only synthetic tokenizer fixtures and equality checks between cached and uncached tokenization, scoped by a `scope: "a"` argument. It shows no production code, key handling, or network surface.

The tests hint at a production prompt-token cache (PromptTokenCaching, cache.encode(text, scope:)) being introduced elsewhere in this PR. That source is not in this batch. It is relevant to A-001 and to the cross-tenant cache and timing-oracle surface in T-041 / SEC-035. The questions for integration are whether the cache is keyed by the coordinator-authored scope, whether it holds plaintext prompt text or token IDs in memory or on disk, and whether it adds a cross-account hit/miss timing channel. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a regression, so I report no findings. Production source for the cache needs review elsewhere, and needs_deeper_review is true because of that coverage gap.
